name: Stams
kurzbeschreibung: Historic site featuring the famous Zisterzienserkloster Stams – the most important cultural monument of the Oberinntal.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stams is situated in the Tyrolean Upper Inntal valley in the district of Imst at an altitude of 671 metres above sea level, spreading across a gravel terrace and the alluvial cone of the Stams stream south of the River Inn. Framed by the rugged limestone peaks of the Mieming Chain to the north and the wooded foothills of the Stubai Alps to the south, the municipality is home to around 1,600 residents. The townscape is dominated by the monumental yellow-and-white facades and twin onion-domed towers of Stams Abbey (Zisterzienserstift Stams). Regarded as the spiritual and cultural heart of the Upper Inntal, Stams is also world-renowned as a training hub for elite winter sports athletes. Surrounded by sunlit fruit orchards, a protected oak forest, and the green ribbon of the Inn, the village harmoniously unites baroque splendour, monastic heritage, and world-class athletic achievement.

Geschichte

Settlement in Stams dates back to pre-Roman times, with its first recorded mention appearing in 1065 in the records of the Bishopric of Brixen as 'Stambs'. A milestone in Tyrolean history occurred in 1272–1273: Count Meinhard II of Gorizia-Tyrol and his wife Elisabeth of Bavaria—widow of Hohenstaufen King Conrad IV and mother of Conradin—founded the Cistercian monastery of Stams as the sovereign burial place and spiritual centre of the County of Tyrol. Following devastation from fires and conflicts, the abbey underwent a glorious baroque transformation in the 17th and 18th centuries under abbots Edmund Zoz and Augustin Neuwirth and court architect Georg Gumpp. The abbey basilica of the Assumption (elevated to Basilica minor in 1983) features the famous early baroque Tree of Life high altar by Bartlmä Steinle with 84 carved saint figurines, alongside the princes' crypt ('Austrian Tomb') adorned with gilded effigies of Tyrolean rulers. In 1967, the Schigymnasium Stams was established, becoming the world's most successful elite sports academy for alpine and nordic winter disciplines.

Anreise

By car, Stams is accessed via the Inntal motorway A12 taking the Mötz/Stams exit (Exit 113), reaching the village centre in two minutes; alternatively, the toll-free federal highway B171 runs directly through the Inntal valley. For rail travellers, the ÖBB railway station Stams along the Arlberg railway line provides excellent connections: S-Bahn Tirol services (lines S1 and S2) and REX regional trains depart from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof every half-hour with a journey time under thirty minutes. VVT regional buses connect Stams seamlessly with Telfs, Mötz, Silz, and Imst. Cyclists reach Stams directly along the long-distance Innradweg R3 cycle route.

Tipps

A tour of Stams Cistercian Abbey is essential: beyond the basilica and princes' tomb, highlights include the opulent Bernardisaal hall with its frescoes and the abbey museum displaying rare religious artworks. In the abbey gardens, the historic Orangerie restaurant offers refined dining, while the abbey shop sells monastic brandies, fruit liqueurs, and herbal products. A scenic pedestrian attraction is the 107-metre suspension bridge spanning the River Inn towards Mötz. Nature enthusiasts can wander through the Stamser Eichenwald, one of the oldest and largest continuous pedunculate oak forests in Central Europe (designated natural monument), complete with ancient trees and a contemplative nature trail. Sports fans should view the Brunnental ski jumping hills at the renowned Schigymnasium Stams.
